text:
Habermas's distinction contrasts law functioning as a steering medium—formal, purposive-rational regulation coordinating systemically integrated spheres like the economy and state administration—with law as an institution, which anchors normative, communicatively integrated spheres of the lifeworld (family, culture, public sphere) in shared values and mutual understanding. Law as medium is instrumental and system-oriented, whereas law as institution preserves normative substance and requires justification through communicative reason. The distinction thus tracks the tension between systemic steering and lifeworld solidarity in modern legal orders.
